content.contents:
'the ballad of yuki' - track 01
what is 'the ballad of yuki'? those of you who've read the artbook may know yuki to be the main character found throughout all of GO UNTIL YOU ARE GONE. as a thank you to chocoa, i wanted to write something for this character, and by extension, him. i wanted the piece to feel like a journey, like one of chopin's ballades or something, and while it pales in comparison, i feel i competently achieved what i set out to do. recording the piano was some of the most fun i've had making an album, ever. i knew i wanted to record an actual piano piece, because whenever i spoke to peers in the community all anybody mentioned was how they liked my keys. here's the thing - almost all of what you hear across static.grl records is programmed piano, not me actually sat there playing. there's a lot of passages that logistically make no sense for hands to be able to play, and while i'm sure if you practiced enough you could probably play some of these pieces, i certainly don't have time to sit down and learn them all, and then play them on a real piano. i don't even have easy access to a real piano, which was part of what made recording this track fun. my girlfriend happened to have a connection in a town nearby - a music school that had a perfectly tuned Yamaha upright waiting to be played. and i really wanted to show i don't just program keys, i play them! i've *been* playing them, since i was a child! so, after spending a few months crafting, writing and practicing, we went and recorded the piece. what you hear on the record is take 9, out of 15 takes we got. we were there pretty much all day!

some photos from the day! the piano was a joy to play. hey, here's an early demo of the track:
https://on.soundcloud.com/P92ooiLRkt6e6k9l8W
you can hear some of the ideas in there but this was a lot of improv, i hadn't fleshed out everything.

'nothing will ever be enough (1)' - track 02
nothing will ever be enough. that's how i felt a lot of the time, especially during this album's creation! call it what you want, imposter syndrome, insecurity, a creeping malaise... there's just this sense i was rife with, that nothing i did, nothing i made, nothing i earned, nothing said would ever be enough for me to believe anything i created, anything that i was or am, would be worth something. i distinctly remember sharing a demo of this song in the digiex demo submissions section of their discord (this was published to digiex's first and only compilation album) and having a constant urge to just delete it alongside all of static.grl because i felt it was all so terrible, worthless. i don't know what had gotten into me, i guess there was just a lot of hopelessness and dejection in the air at the time. i'd just moved back to the UK, the election and the news surrounding it was nothing but misery, i couldn't find a job to save my life and it was the middle of winter, when my cyclical depression tends to reach its peak. when the compilation was released, a few people reached out saying they loved my track, and moreover a very close friend - simvlacrvm- encouraged me to keep going. he saw something in me, quite a few people did, something i was blind to. then, only a couple months later, i managed to score a record deal for the upcoming album. i started to believe, hey, maybe *i* am enough.
i always liked how that one track by 2star starts with auto-panned drums, so i like to include that in my tracks. there's quite a few samples on this track, i won't spell them out for y'all but they're in there. one, towards the end, is from a very talented californian guitarist, who could also be the protag of a very popular game series. :3c

'the oppressor (there is no punishment befitting)' - track 03
who is the oppressor? anybody who has had to live in the groping grasp of the male gaze knows the answer. that's precisely what this track is about. the sampling reflects this. the song is just venting, i suppose, about my frustrations with what masculinity is poised (advertised?) to be. strong, hard, misogynistic, penetrative, violating, crude. that's how i wanted the track to sound, too, and i'd say it succeeds. i guess it was also kind of, what if static.grl... but death grips? LOL
which, it doesn't achieve at all, but i've always appreciated more experimental mixing and synthesis, so i wanted to throw my hat in the ring. in terms of the album's overall 'story' (a term i use loosely), i suppose this is the moment we realize one cannot live beyond this gaze, we can only learn to try and ignore it, and hope that in future we may educate those with open minds. so first, we have a lament from yuki in her ballad, then she tells us further how nothing will ever be enough for her to believe life is worth something, and then she shares what's made her feel this way (I.E., the oppressor).

'girls in my dreams are made up of static interference' - track 04
this was one of the hardest tracks to work on. it took forever to get the mix sounding right, but i learned a lot in the process about how to make each element of a mix stand out using EQ, etc. as such, it's ended up being a favorite of mine. the sample at the beginning i think flows well from the preceding track's theme, and sums up my feelings quite well. sometimes, it *is* just easier to run. the piano in this track is possibly some of my favorite work i've composed. i just think it's quite emotional and pretty :3
it's a weird title. i guess girls being made up of static interference is, as well as being a lain reference, indicative of love being but temporary, like a flash on a screen. love from a partner feels dreamlike, something tangible mentally but unachievable in any real, physical sense. of course, they're also made of static, because *i* am :D i'm the static girl!!!!!!111

'i have a hole in my chest' - track 05
this was one of the earliest paintings i was sent by chocoa, and i loved the representation of trauma as a hole in one's chest. it's incredibly apt, and when i saw this phrase written out as above, i knew that had to be a title of one of the album's tracks. the sample from the beginning is actually from a fugazi gig. i fucking love that band. i had recently heard Midori's 'How to Build a Nuclear Bomb [etc.]', which started with a very cool, atmosphere-building quote, and i just loved the vibes across that record, so i attempted to write something in that vein. i had a challenge getting the sounds right - in particular, that insane synthesizer that sweeps from left to write was originally a pad that just sounded like garbage no matter what i did to it. so, in the end, i added a bunch of distortion and some sweeping panning and it ended up sounding kind of insane so i rolled with it. this was my first time using an acid bass (or 303), and i actually designed it in serum specifically for this track. i've since used it a lot, but this was its first use. in hindsight, i probably would've changed how it's mixed a little bit, but i'm overall very happy with the chaos this track permeates, and i think it works really well where it's at in the album's layout!

'this creeping malaise' - track 06
if i don't stand my own ground, how can i find my way out of this maze?
when everything is falling apart around you, it becomes so easy to blame yourself. especially when the media consistently tells you how much of an awful inconvenience you are. media funded by a government that is just as happy to repeat that notion. it feels like the path of least resistence. like a twisted, abusive comfort.
but, there's something that creeps up on you, consistently, a feeling that won't leave, an itch that can't be scratched, something that tells you that life must change in order for it to continue. that change starts in the midst of this track. everything is chaotic, depressive, nothing feels real, validating, tangible. then comes a moment of slowdown, a moment of clarity, where things start to fall into place, concepts feel less elusive, more comprehensible. suddenly, something makes sense. change will occur. it will wash upon you as sure as the tide brings the seawater to kiss the sand. and as the last notes fade away... there is the genesis of a sacred evolution.

'cocoon (mind with whom you speak)' - track 07
this track was inspired by 2814, who i've loved for nearly 10 years now. ambient soundcapes just do something for me. so, i wanted to make something similar that was inkeeping with the album's themes, and chocoa wanted yuki to become a moth. i thought it was a great allegory for, well, y'know. so to put the listener in an evolutionary standstill (a cocoon) felt very natural. it's a moment of rest, of clarity, of introspection, of respite. considering all that comes before and after this track, i think it's well-earned. i think towards the end it gets a bit like, 80s-cheesy, maybe too cyberpunk/vangelis, but i also love HOME, so i really like those traditional synthesizer sounds, and i thought they'd work well to cut through as a lead in the mix. it definitely needed something like that, otherwise it would've felt like the track had no progression!

'becoming now a moth (away this silken paper coat)' - track 08 [feat. simvlacrvm]
a moth is not by any stretch of the imagination a fascimile of a butterfly, the two are separate, but similar, serialized under the same category entomologically speaking. though the process through which each larva becomes pupa and then achieves adulthood is much the same. i wonder what this could be analogous of?
a slow fade, like coming out of your cocoon, followed by impactful and exciting beats! it all shows you how badass you feel when you wash off the dirt thrown your way. this track was another i was stuck on for a while, mainly because a lot of the track was handled by simvlacrvm. eventually i worked out where my parts would work best though, and now it definitely feels like a good harmony between our two styles. i asked him to add a few words, here's what he had to say:

'And So You Will Go Until You Are Gone (2)' - track 09
this track has a two at the end, and similarly “nothing will ever be enough” has a one. i wonder if the two tracks are connected in some way? i wonder if the phrases are connected...?
i believe this was the first track i fully completed for the album. i must've finished it back in February or March. i'd been listening to a lot of squarepusher and i loved how he chopped his beats, so i tried to emulate that. of course, it's nowhere near his level, but i think i did my own thing with it. this was the first track i made, too, where i felt i was officially 'back on the grind'. after so much perceived stagnation, it felt good to make something i was at least somewhat proud of. the track almost feels like a fakeout in how it starts almost lo-fi beats adjacent, then goes into more heavy breaks later on. most of the samples you hear come off of the legendary CD sample-pack used by Akira Yamaoka on Silent Hill 2. i wonder if there's any other SH2 samples across the record?
the opening two chords also sound awfully familiar. i wonder where else one may have heard them?

'A Prison of/is Your Own Creation' - track 10
Even if no one understands me, I am a human being.
as such, a prison is your own creation. chains that bind us can be reduced to but proverbial. although there's limitations within a hierarchical societal structure, to push those boundaries is to be free. and i don't know about you, but i want to be free. in the essence of that freedom, of pushing the definitions of a preconceived, selfish status-quo, one can find true, radical self-love. and that is what i have found, outside of the prison. i hope everyone on this earth may too find it.
this track stagnated for a short while, but once i introduced some more spliced beats and the piano parts, it really started to take shape. i knew i wanted guitar somewhere on the record - actually, there was originally going to be a singy-song on it, you can hear that here: https://on.soundcloud.com/vXwmUAkoy9YPJaJJ7H (TW / title is... what it is. lyrics elude to S/A, gr**ming etc). not only would this track have been out of place, i also think the title is too on-the-nose and upsetting. instead, i decided to put some guitar on the last track. the guitar used is a very old (nearly 100y/o!) classical guitar, the one my grandfather learned on. it was him who convinced my mom to get me piano lessons when i was 6, so to hear my piano playing alongside the guitar that was his at the very end feels very culminative. the less digital-sounding piano you hear there (the very end) is, incidentally, the same piano we used for recording the ballad of yuki. we had some time leftover so, i recorded that ending passage. i wasn't sure if it would sound good in the mix, but as all is said and done i think it definitely works. this is probably my favorite track on the record. the message behind it means a lot to me and i just love how everything came together. there's even... well, those who bought the vinyl will see. i've always been a sucker for bonus/hidden tracks.

that concludes my writings on GUYAG2013. overall, it's my proudest work to date and i love it to pieces. i want to thank DDB for hosting my album, i want to thank chocoa for sticking with me and writing something beautiful as a companion piece to my music, and i want to thank every one of you from the bottom of my heart for listening to this album, and hearing my voice. this album is me, in almost every aspect. when it came to writing it, i knew from the moment it was going to be pressed to vinyl that what i wanted to do more than anything is lean into myself. being presented with such a beautiful, privileged opportunity wasn't something i wanted to take lightly, and it gave me the confidence i desperately needed to make something i'd be happy with, something i didn't have to sacrifice shit for, something i could lean into myself throughout, something that means something to me, something that was enough. now, i can safely say, i have something that is enough. this album is enough. those who listen to it, they're enough. you've all taught me that i'm worth something, that what i make is worth something, that maybe i can actually make music i'm proud of, that people will want to listen to and enjoy. i sincerely love you all.
if for whatever reason you have any other questions regarding the album (or just generally), please email me at static.grl.digital@gmail.com
